root.name: Ruy Lopez: Vinogradov Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Qe7

overview: Black answers 3.Bb5 with 3...Qe7, defending e5 with the queen instead of ...a6 or ...Nf6. White usually plays 4.O-O or 4.c3 and builds a centre with d4, or 4.Bxc6 dxc6 5.d4. The queen on e7 blocks the bishop and develops awkwardly, so White is comfortably better.

white_ideas.idea: Castle, play c3 and d4 and build a broad centre
Exchange on c6 and attack e5 when the queen is passive

black_ideas.idea: Defend e5 solidly and develop with ...Nf6 and ...d6
Aim to break with ...d5 once pieces are out

typical_structures.structure: Ruy Lopez centre with e4/d4 against e5/d6
Exchange structure after Bxc6 dxc6 with an open d-file

character.notes: Quiet, slow development; Black is passive but safe.

soundness.notes: Playable but passive and a little worse; not refuted.

structure.notes: The e5 pawn is held under tension against e4.

approach.notes: A rare Black sideline that strong players seldom use.

level.notes: Standard Ruy Lopez plans; low theory burden.

character.reason: Black keeps e5 protected and sits passively, with few ways to lose quickly.

soundness.reason: Slightly worse for Black but not refuted.

structure.reason: e4 against e5 stays in tension while White builds with c3 and d4.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom play 3...Qe7; less used than other side lines.

level.reason: Ordinary Ruy Lopez ideas, little theory.

plans.reason: White builds a bigger centre against a passive set-up.
